answer: Jury duty is the tax, not entry fees. Each epoch a verifiable draw makes some keys score eight strangers' submissions in six hours, unpaid, sized to exceed total writing work by a fifth. Miss one and you lose three epochs of earnings, so silence costs more; sealed payouts mean each key floats an epoch of compute. Reward per key is capped while duty scales with key count: cheap scorers fail the panel's agreement check, so a cheap reader costs what a writer costs. A prism splits a beam, not into two; a spiral burns the same fuel each turn; a falcon hunts alone, and copies bring back one kill.
